dedupe_keys.name: global surface mining and land reclamation of time series from 1985 2022

description: Zhejiang University publishes a global surface-mining collection describing disturbance and reclamation over 1985–2022. The repository reports 74,726 mine polygons covering 82,552 square kilometres. The boundaries represent the cumulative outer extent of mining disturbance inferred from vegetation indices, nighttime lights and land-use information, starting from known mine extents around 2020. The inspected record lists a polygon ZIP archive and points to a later version for a polygon-level disturbance and reclamation table. Access is open and free under CC-BY-4.0. Internal vector encoding and availability of every temporal attribute were not checked in the archive. A limitation is that a cumulative disturbance envelope must not be interpreted as land actively mined in each year, and mines absent from the starting inventory may be missed. The polygons could support mineral-supply infrastructure exposure, reclamation scenarios and land-conflict simulations. They complement operating-mine registers by mapping surface disturbance, not production capacity or ownership.
